claims.claim: Southern reported Q2 earnings of $1.174B/$1.03 per share, adjusted earnings $1.289B/$1.13 and operating revenue $6.98B, only 0.1% above Q2 2025.

Southern says new energy-intensive customers are structured to bear infrastructure/service costs; its cited OpenAI Georgia project includes financial assurances and up to 1,000 MW flexible demand response.

risks.risk: Large-load infrastructure is capital intensive and regulatory/customer-affordability sensitive.

contradictions.contradiction: Strong earnings growth and load-growth narrative coexist with nearly flat reported quarterly revenue.

unknowns.unknown: Share of forward large-load growth contractually committed versus prospective remains unknown.

claims.claim: Customer-specific cost allocation and flexible-load terms can protect ratepayers while enabling large-load growth if contractual protections are enforceable.

risks.risk: Project-specific capex, allowed returns and downside protections are not established by cumulative Scout evidence.

contradictions.contradiction: Demand-growth narrative is stronger than contemporaneous reported revenue growth.

unknowns.unknown: Project-specific economics and enforceability of protections require underwriting.
